subject: Data handling follow-up: retention models & evidence
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Ghosh <samir.ghosh@datasentry.io>, Elena Park <elena.park@datasentry.io>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 09 Aug 2026 16:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call follow-up — data handling options and proposed next steps

Hi Samir / Elena,

Thanks again for taking the time today — really helpful to understand Datasentry's architecture and the compliance constraints around patient PII and EU residency. Below is a short recap of the asks we captured and three concrete options we can propose for your legal/security review. I attached a one-page proposal (redwood-retention-proposal-v1.pdf) with more detail.

Key asks we captured
- Zero/near-zero retention of raw user conversation content (customer expects no persistent storage of PII).
- Explicit handling of KV cache and intermediate model context (clarify if these are considered "logs").
- Evidence for deletion / SOC 2 artifacts and dataflow diagram for internal audits.
- Preference for a deployment option that supports strict data locality (US/EU).

Proposed options (high level)
1) Private / Dedicated (recommended for strict 0-retention):
   - Option to run Redwood Private with customer-managed control plane or dedicated capacity.
   - Logs disabled by default; query-level ephemeral handling (no persistent transcript).
   - We can provide deletion attestations and on-premise dataflow diagrams.
2) Hosted with short retention windows (production-friendly):
   - Token-level logs for 7 days only; metrics/aggregates retained longer (30–90 days).
   - PII redaction pipeline applied before long-term storage.
3) Hybrid: TTL carveouts per route + selective KV retention
   - Keep KV cache for active sessions only; flush on session end.
   - Maintain short 0–3 day window for sensitive routes; 30 days for non-PII analytics.

Immediate next steps I propose
- I will send the security packet (SOC2 summary + dataflow) and the retention proposal attached.
- Marissa will help coordinate a short technical deep-dive with our infra/SE team to walk through KV semantics and deletion behavior.
- If Datasentry prefers Private, we can scope timeline & pricing for a dedicated pilot.

Ask for you: could you confirm which of the three options looks feasible from a compliance perspective, and please share the name/email of the compliance lead who should get the SOC2 packet?

Thanks — happy to set times for a tech call next week.

Best,
Ben Carter
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0198

Attachment: redwood-retention-proposal-v1.pdf

From: Samir Ghosh <samir.ghosh@datasentry.io>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: Elena Park <elena.park@datasentry.io>
Date: Mon, 10 Aug 2026 09:34:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call follow-up — data handling options and proposed next steps

Ben —

Thanks for the clear recap. Quick clarifications before we loop in our legal/compliance folks:

1) When you say "KV cache" (option 3), does that include embeddings/indices we persist for retrieval augmentation? We need to know whether those are considered "stored user data".
2) For the hosted 7-day window, is the 7-day retention applied to raw transcript only, or also to intermediate artifacts (token-level logs, model prompts, assistant responses)?
3) The customer success team asked whether you can provide a deletion proof (audit record) when data is purged. An automated deletion event with a verifiable timestamp would be ideal.

Elena (cc) is our Head of Compliance — she'll want to see the SOC 2 Type II summary and a dataflow diagram. Also, we have a strict requirement that PII is never stored in plain text at rest. Is token-level encryption with customer-managed KMS an option for hosted?

Happy to join a technical call — afternoons PST next week work best.

—Samir
Samir Ghosh
Head of Engineering, Datasentry
samir.ghosh@datasentry.io

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Ghosh <samir.ghosh@datasentry.io>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 10 Aug 2026 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call follow-up — data handling options and proposed next steps

Samir — thanks, good questions. Looping Aditya (solutions) and Marissa (CS) so we can get concrete technical language and timelines on each point. Answers below and proposed playbook: 

Short answers
- KV vs embeddings: We treat persistent embeddings/indices as customer-managed artifacts when you enable retrieval augmentation. If Datasentry wants zero-storage for anything derived from PII, we recommend disabling persistent embeddings and relying on session-scoped caches only.
- 7-day hosted window: The 7-day scope applies to raw transcripts and token-level logs captured for debugging. Intermediate artifacts (embeddings, indices) are excluded unless you explicitly enable persistence.
- Deletion proof: We can emit an auditable deletion event (log entry with timestamp and object id) and include it in an export. For Private/Dedicated pilots we can provide a signed deletion attestation from the host node.
- KMS: Hosted supports customer-managed KMS for data at rest (enterprise plan). For the highest assurance, Private allows you to manage keys in your VPC/HSM.

Proposed technical playbook (concrete)
1) Security packet: We will send SOC2 summary, dataflow diagram, and a short note on redaction behavior by EOD.
2) Tech deep-dive (30–45m): Aditya to demo how KV is scoped per session and where persistent artifacts may be stored. Proposed slots: Tue 08/11 10:00–10:45 PST or Wed 08/12 14:00–14:45 PST.
3) Pilot scoping: If you prefer Private/Dedicated for the pilot, we’ll prepare an estimate (capacity + ops) and an internal checklist for setup time (expect 3–6 weeks for a minimal dedicated pilot).

Next steps for you
- Please confirm which time works for the deep-dive and whether your compliance team prefers an NDA before we share the full SOC2 package.

Marissa will coordinate scheduling. Aditya — please attach the short KV behavior note to the packet and include exact retention keys implemented by Redwood (prefixes, object ids we will purge).

Ben
Ben Carter
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.ai

Attachment: datasentry-discovery-notes.pdf

From: Elena Park <elena.park@datasentry.io>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Samir Ghosh <samir.ghosh@datasentry.io>
Date: Tue, 11 Aug 2026 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call follow-up — data handling options and proposed next steps

Ben / Samir —

Thanks for the detail. We want to move quickly: Tue 08/11 10:00 PST works for us (please send calendar invite). We also need an NDA before our legal team will accept SOC2 docs — can you send a standard mutual NDA or a DocuSign link?

One note on scope: if Private/Dedicated is the only path to full zero-retention, please include a conservative timeline and a pilot budget ballpark in your follow-up — we’ll evaluate internally but will prioritize the option that gives us strongest control over data at rest.

Elena Park
Head of Compliance, Datasentry
elena.park@datasentry.io
